triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module granted the $32 telephone standard allowance to every household that merely failed to qualify for the heating/cooling or utilities allowances, omitting the source's requirement that the allowance consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone — i.e. that the household actually incurred or anticipated such a cost.
triage.triage_notes: Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us-ny/regulation/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/c): text confirms 'The standard allowance for telephone consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone', so the added conjunct is source-grounded, not new unclaimed scope. Decisive diff: eligibility formula changed from 'not snap_heating_cooling_standard_allowance_eligible and not snap_utilities_standard_allowance_eligible' to the same two negations ANDed with the new input household_incurred_or_anticipated_basic_service_cost_for_one_telephone; snap_individual_utility_allowance was rewritten to a nested if-chain that also gates on that input, so a household without telephone cost now yields 0 instead of 32. Companion test regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/c.test.yaml adds case 'no_telephone_basic_service_cost_prevents_telephone_allowance' expecting snap_individual_utility_allowance: 0, and policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.test.yaml pins the new input to false in its shared base case — behavioral change confirmed, not cosmetic. The commit ALSO made non-fidelity changes in the same module: (a) the module summary was replaced with verbatim regulation text (provenance/mechanical); (b) the parameter was renamed ny_snap_telephone_utility_allowance_amount -> telephone_standard_allowance_amount with the same 32 value, effective_from 2025-10-01 and dtype/unit unchanged (rename only); (c) the rule snap_telephone_allowance_eligible was renamed to snap_telephone_standard_allowance_eligible; (d) the source_relation rule 'sets_snap_telephone_utility_allowance' (a 'sets' relation onto us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option with a delegation basis) was DROPPED entirely and not replaced — that removes a cross-reference/delegation assertion rather than a computed value, so I did not treat it as the defect, but a reviewer may want to check whether losing that relation was intended. Evidence quality caveat: the commit body is empty and the subject is generic ('Regenerate NY SNAP telephone allowance'); the attached PR (#395) is the unrelated US monorepo-consolidation PR that absorbed this history via git subtree, so its body/reviews say nothing about this change. The only text that names the defect is the post-fix module summary quoting the regulation, hence confidence held below 0.8. The encoding manifest (.axiom/encoding-manifests/.../c.json) records a supervised encoder run (openai-gpt-5.5 backend, run dir axiom-encode-ny-telephone-11) but carries no prose rationale.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix formula for `snap_telephone_allowance_eligible` was `not snap_heating_cooling_standard_allowance_eligible and not snap_utilities_standard_allowance_eligible`, so any household failing the other two standards received the $32 telephone allowance; the fix adds a required conjunct `household_incurred_or_anticipated_basic_service_cost_for_one_telephone` and threads the same gate through `snap_individual_utility_allowance`, which is an encoded-meaning change, not bookkeeping. The pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-ny-snap-2026-07-17, record a14d03c7) confirms the source's first sentence — "The standard allowance for telephone consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone." — which the pre-fix encoding represented nowhere, and the companion test adds `no_telephone_basic_service_cost_prevents_telephone_allowance` asserting not_holds / 0 where the old module returned 32. I tried to refute this as amount/date/entity (all unchanged: $32, effective_from 2025-10-01, Household/SnapUnit), as polarity (no operator inverted — a conjunct was added), and as mechanical (renames and the summary-to-regulation-text swap are present but ride alongside a real formula change), and none of those hold; the only surviving counter-reading is that the first sentence is definitional rather than an eligibility gate, which the sibling provisions (a)/(b) incurrence tests make unlikely.
triage.verifier_notes: Commit message is bare ("Regenerate NY SNAP telephone allowance", empty body) — the "(screen-flagged)" sentence in the task brief is screening output, not maintainer text, so the evidence here is the diff, the companion test, and the resolved source text, not a quoted admission. Two other changes ride in the same regeneration and a reviewer should look at them separately: (1) the commit deletes the `source_relation` rule `sets_snap_telephone_utility_allowance`, which had target `us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` with a delegation basis — that is a coverage/linkage removal, not part of the reviewed defect, and it is the one plausible candidate for a competing kind (untraceable_branch or wrong_entity_or_scope) if a reviewer thinks the relation, not the eligibility gate, is the decisive edit; (2) renames (`ny_snap_telephone_utility_allowance_amount` → `telephone_standard_allowance_amount`, `snap_telephone_allowance_eligible` → `snap_telephone_standard_allowance_eligible`) and the summary replacement are mechanical noise that should not be read as additional defects. Residual risk on the kind: the added gate is grounded in a definitional sentence ("consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone") rather than an explicit "is available only to households which incur…" clause, so a strict reader could call the new input an interpretive addition; I weigh that as minority because (a) and (b) in the same subdivision both gate on incurred cost and the added input name mirrors (a)'s `household_incurred_or_anticipated_heating_or_cooling_costs_separate_from_rent_or_mortgage`.
